title: Uniqueness of transonic shock solutions modulo a translation in an approximate nozzle
author: Minghong Han, Bingsong Long, Hairong Yuan
work: Uniqueness of transonic shock solutions in general approximate nozzles for steady potential flow
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's main theorem, published as Theorem 1.1 (Main theorem): for given uniform supersonic inflow, the free boundary problem for the steady potential flow equation (an elliptic-hyperbolic mixed type equation) on the sphere has a transonic shock solution if and only if the exit speed equals the constant u_1 determined by the data, and that solution is unique modulo a translation of the shock. The unit is not a qualification exercise because the counted claim cannot be reached without the whole source-local analysis that the unit retains and that the proof body carries: the reduction of the flow to a Cauchy problem for a nonlinear ordinary differential equation by Bernoulli's law, the construction of the symmetric background solution and the proof that its shock location is not determined (the chain rule computation through the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions, equation (2.6) and the identity (2.8)), the linearisation of the mass conservation equation about the background solution with its uniformly elliptic coefficient matrix and the first-order terms, the boundary conditions on the exit and on the shock, the sign claim psi <= 0 on the shock obtained by integrating the difference of the two background velocity fields, and then the global argument itself: the strong maximum principle with the Hopf boundary point lemma in the two cases u_1 >= c_theta_1 and u_1 < c_theta_1, including the normal-derivative contradiction at a minimum on the shock, whose justification is deferred to Remark 2.4 and carried out there by a second integral comparison. Proving uniqueness modulo translation for a transonic shock free boundary problem in a curved approximate nozzle is research-level nonlinear partial differential equations, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
